title: Sequential-merge facets for two-dimensional group problems
contribution: Introduces the sequential-merge operation that combines two one-dimensional group facets into facets of the two-dimensional group problem, giving large families of MIP cuts (abstract).
problem_entry: Strong cuts for unstructured MIPs via two-dimensional group problems instead of one-row relaxations (abstract).
key_idea: Sequential merge of two one-dimensional facet-defining inequalities yields two-dimensional facets; any one-dimensional constituents allowed (abstract).
positioning: Builds on the Dey-Richard three-gradient facet (abstract).
limits_future: Cuts with stronger continuous-variable coefficients than one-dimensional cuts; recovers the three-gradient facet of Dey and Richard (abstract).

method_links.note: pre-QCQP form: two-row MILP relaxation asked what one-row theory knows

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: compose lower-dimensional facets into higher-dimensional ones
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: sequential merge of two 1-D group facets

transferable: Build higher-dimensional valid inequalities by an operation composing known lower-dimensional facets, so an existing library of 1-D results transfers at once (abstract).

quotes.text: We present a new operation that generates facet-defining inequalities for two-dimensional group problems by combining two facet-defining inequalities of one-dimensional group problems.

title: Strong cutting planes for unstructured mixed integer programs using multiple constraints
contribution: PhD thesis: first facet families for the two-dimensional group problem and an LP-based approximate lifting method for cuts using multiple constraints (abstract).
problem_entry: Cuts for unstructured MIPs using several constraints simultaneously, extending group and lifting approaches (abstract).
key_idea: Extreme-function properties of infinite group problems; two linear-time facet families for the 2-D group problem; approximate lifting coefficients from at most two LPs, applied to Glover's primal algorithm (abstract).
experiments: Gap closed by new two-row cuts versus GMI cuts alone and versus aggregation; lifting tested in Glover's primal algorithm (abstract).
limits_future: One family explains the empirical success of aggregation-based cut generation; claimed best known performance for a cutting-plane primal algorithm (abstract).

method_links.note: theoretical explanation for the empirical success of aggregation-based cut generation
multi-row MILP version of the substructure paradigm

transferable: Replace an exact lifting problem (a nonlinear MIP) by an LP-computable approximation and test it inside a concrete algorithm (abstract).

quotes.text: The first family provides a theoretical explanation for the empirical success of aggregation-based cut-generation schemes.

title: Lifting integer variables in minimal inequalities corresponding to lattice-free triangles
contribution: Characterizes lifting functions for integer variables in minimal two-row inequalities from lattice-free triangles: unique for two triangle categories, not necessarily unique for the third (abstract).
problem_entry: Two-row minimal inequalities (Andersen et al.; Borozan-Cornuejols) cover only continuous variables; tableau use needs lifting of integer variables (abstract).
key_idea: Classify maximal lattice-free triangles into three categories and analyse lifting in each; use the Johnson fill-in inequality for the third (abstract).
positioning: Extends Andersen et al. and Borozan-Cornuejols to integer variables (abstract).
limits_future: Sufficient conditions for fill-in minimality and conditions for extremality in the third category (abstract).

method_links.note: uniqueness proved for two categories, shown to fail in the third

quotes.text: We show that the lifting function is not necessarily unique in the third category.

title: The group-theoretic approach in mixed integer programming
contribution: Survey chapter on the group-theoretic approach in MIP: geometry of group relaxations, structure, valid-inequality derivation, extremality proof techniques, computational insights (abstract).
problem_entry: Overview of foundations and advances of the group-theoretic approach (abstract).
key_idea: Geometric motivation of group relaxations, optimization over them, valid inequalities for master group relaxations and general extremality proof techniques (abstract).
limits_future: Ends with computational evidence on the strength of group relaxations and cuts (abstract).
transferable: In a survey, close with computational evidence on the strength of the relaxation as the check on the theory (abstract).

title: Experiments with two row tableau cuts
contribution: Computational test of two-row cuts from type-2 lattice-free triangles against one round of GMI cuts on random instance classes (abstract).
problem_entry: After much theory on two-row group relaxations, test effectiveness of triangle cuts (abstract).
key_idea: Heuristic triangle generation plus lifting of integer coefficients; compare gap closed in one round against GMI cuts (abstract).
experiments: Randomly generated instance classes varying number of integer non-basic variables, bounds and non-negativity; one-round gap closed versus GMI (abstract).
limits_future: A first step in testing triangle cuts; results not stated in the abstract (abstract).

method_links.note: stripped one-round gap-closed comparison on random classes varying one feature at a time

coauthors: Andrea Lodi, Andrea Tramontani, Laurence A. Wolsey

quotes.text: Our tests are carried out on different classes of randomly generated instances designed to represent different models in the literature by varying the number of integer non-basic variables, bounds and non-negativity constraints.

title: The Chvátal-Gomory closure of an ellipsoid is a polyhedron
contribution: Proves the CG closure of a rational bounded full-dimensional ellipsoid is a rational polytope, the first extension of CG-closure polyhedrality to a non-polyhedral set (abstract).
problem_entry: CG closure of a rational polyhedron is polyhedral; does it extend to non-polyhedral convex sets (abstract)?
key_idea: Every non-integral boundary point is separated by a constructed sequence of CG cuts; polyhedrality then follows by compactness (abstract).
limits_future: Also yields sufficient conditions for general compact convex sets (abstract).

method_links.note: MILP closure result asked of a convex nonlinear set

transferable: Reduce a polyhedrality claim to separating every boundary point by some cut, then close with compactness (abstract).

quotes.text: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first extension of the polyhedrality of the CG closure to a non-polyhedral set.

title: Collaborative Research: Fundamentals of Convex Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
contribution: NSF award abstract: programme to extend five MILP results (hull representation, value functions, strong duals, subadditive cuts, CG/split closures) to convex MINLP (abstract).
problem_entry: No general-purpose convex MINLP solvers comparable to MILP (abstract).
key_idea: Carry convex-hull representation, value-function subadditivity, strong duality, subadditive cuts and elementary closures from MILP to convex MINLP (abstract).
limits_future: Planned research; expected to aid branch-and-cut for convex MINLP (abstract).

method_links.note: MILP checklist asked of convex MINLP as the stated project objective

transferable: Write the research programme as an explicit list of results known for the simpler class, each asked of the harder class (abstract).

quotes.text: The research objective of this project is to broaden the scope of the following key results known for MILP to the more general domain of convex MINLP

title: CAREER: Non-traditional Cutting-Plane Algorithms for Mixed-Integer Programs
contribution: NSF CAREER award abstract: non-traditional cutting-plane paradigms (multi-constraint cuts, design-then-verify, enumeration-guided cuts) plus an OR puzzle competition and a graduate course (abstract).
problem_entry: Information useful for cut derivation and selection is left unused by MIP solvers (abstract).
key_idea: Three paradigms: multiple constraints at once; design cuts then verify validity; explicit enumeration of integer points to guide cuts (abstract).

method_links.note: explicit enumeration of integer points to guide cut choice

quotes.text: Design suitable cutting planes and then verify their validity before use, instead of deriving cutting planes without any control over their quality.

title: A polynomial-time algorithm to check closedness of simple second order mixed-integer sets
contribution: Polynomial-time algorithm to decide closedness of the convex hull of simple second-order conic mixed-integer sets, with sufficient conditions for intersections in the pure integer case (abstract).
problem_entry: Closedness of integer hulls, automatic for rational polyhedra, asked of Lorentz-cone mixed-integer sets (abstract).
key_idea: Polynomial-time closedness test for simple SOCMISs (abstract).
limits_future: Only sufficient conditions for intersections of simple SOCMISs (pure integer) (abstract).

method_links.note: MILP hull property asked of conic mixed-integer sets
weak: intersection case left at sufficient conditions

quotes.text: We show that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm to check the closedness of the convex hull of simple SOCMISs.

title: Sparse Integer Programming
contribution: NSF award abstract: study mathematical implications of sparse constraint matrices in MILP to explain observed solver behaviour and design sparsity-exploiting methods (abstract).
problem_entry: Sparsity is under-explored for MILP algorithms despite sparse formulations in practice (abstract).
key_idea: Seek formal explanations for sparse cut selection, feasibility pump on sparse MILPs and integral-vertex frequency in sparse binary formulations (abstract).
limits_future: Planned: sparse cut selection paradigm, extended formulations for sparsity, heuristics for sparse instances; one PhD student (abstract).

method_links.note: stated aim is formal explanation of empirically observed solver behaviour, three habits named

quotes.text: If successful, this project will be able to uncover formal mathematical explanation for various empirically observed behavior of mixed-integer linear programs, such as: Why does selection of sparse cutting-planes for mixed-integer linear programs with sparse constraint matrix work well in many cases?

title: MIPLearn: an extensible framework for learning-enhanced optimization
contribution: MIPLearn software: ML learns patterns from previously solved instances to accelerate commercial MIP solvers while keeping optimality proofs (abstract).
problem_entry: Repeatedly solved problem families have regularities general MIP solvers ignore (abstract).
key_idea: Learn redundant constraints and typical variable values from past instances and pass them to CPLEX/Gurobi/XPRESS (abstract).
limits_future: Benefits claimed only for certain classes of problems (abstract).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: learn instance-family regularities but keep the solver certificate
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: MIPLearn keeps optimality and feasibility proofs

coauthors: Alinson S. Xavier, Feng Qiu, Xiaoyi Gu, Berkay Becu

quotes.text: Unlike pure ML methods, MIPLearn is not only able to find high-quality solutions to discrete optimization problems, but it can also prove the optimality and feasibility of these solutions.

title: Combined Bound Tightening on McCormick Relaxations of AC Optimal Power Flow
contribution: Combines SOCP-based bound tightening, valid inequalities (ring cuts, reverse cone and arctangent envelopes) and FBBT on McCormick LP relaxations of ACOPF, halving the average SOCP gap (abstract).
problem_entry: Strengthen LP relaxations of ACOPF by combining valid inequalities with FBBT (abstract).
key_idea: McCormick envelopes on the SOCP relaxation; bound tightening via SOCP first, then valid inequalities and successive McCormick refinement with FBBT (abstract).
experiments: Average SOCP gap 8.14% to 4.11%; test set not stated in abstract (abstract).
limits_future: Arctangent envelopes with FBBT give a tighter and more scalable relaxation (abstract).

method_links.note: cheap LP relaxation strengthened by structure-derived inequalities with certified gap as deliverable

coauthors: X. An, C. Crozier, S. Grijalva

quotes.text: This approach significantly reduces the average SOCP gap from 8.14% to 4.11%, thereby improving the practical performance of convex relaxations for ACOPF.
